h1: The 4 Best Battery Backpack Leaf Blowers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Backpack Leaf Blowers 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: four battery backpack leaf blowers from WORX and Greenworks, compared on airflow, voltage and who each one suits.
summary: The WORX Backpack Leaf Blower is our all-around pick for yards that outgrow a handheld. The Greenworks 40V is the airflow leader on paper at 660 CFM, while the Greenworks 60V and Greenworks Pro 60-Volt both list 550 CFM for buyers who want a higher-voltage platform. All four sit in the $200 to $500 range.
intro: The biggest mistake with a battery backpack blower is shopping the CFM number alone. A blower that moves a lot of air but hangs badly on your back gets used for ten minutes and then retired to the garage. The harness and the platform matter as much as the headline airflow.

We reviewed the backpack models in this price band and ranked them on the spec sheets and the details each listing gives. Four true backpack designs made the cut, all from WORX and Greenworks, and every one sits in the $200 to $500 bucket. Handheld blowers were left out because they are a different tool.

products.name: WORX Backpack Leaf Blower
products.verdict: The safe default for a yard that is too big for a handheld.
products.description:
The WORX Backpack Leaf Blower is a battery-powered backpack design in the $200 to $500 range. The listing is short on numbers, so the case for it rests on the format itself: weight carried on your back instead of in your wrist.

It takes the top spot because it gives no reason to hesitate. The Greenworks models below publish airflow figures, and the 40V version lists a higher one, but a bigger number on paper is not the same as a better day of yard work.

Buy it if you want a straightforward backpack blower from a well known tool brand. The caveat is that the listing shows no CFM figure, so check the airflow on the product page before you commit.
products.idealFor: Homeowners with a larger yard who want a backpack blower without fuss.
products.skipIf: You want a published airflow number before buying.

products.name: Greenworks 40V Backpack Leaf Blower
products.verdict: The highest listed airflow of the four backpack picks.
products.description:
The Greenworks 40V Backpack Leaf Blower lists 660 CFM, the highest airflow figure among the backpack models here. It is a battery backpack unit in the $200 to $500 range.

It ranks just under the WORX because a 40V platform is a lower voltage than the 60V Greenworks models below it, so the airflow lead comes with a different battery system rather than a bigger one. That is the real tradeoff to weigh.

Choose it if moving more air is your priority and you do not already own 60V batteries. The caveat is that CFM alone does not describe air speed, which the listing does not give.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want the most listed airflow in a backpack blower.

products.name: Greenworks 60V Backpack Leaf Blower
products.verdict: A 60V backpack blower with a clearly stated 550 CFM.
products.description:
The Greenworks 60V Backpack Leaf Blower lists 550 CFM and a backpack design, in the $200 to $500 range.

It sits below the 40V model because it lists 110 fewer CFM, even though the voltage is higher. It sits above the Pro 60-Volt model because its listing is clearer about what you are getting and carries a simpler name.

It suits buyers committed to a 60V battery system. The caveat is that on paper you give up airflow compared with the 660 CFM Greenworks above.
products.skipIf: Maximum airflow matters more than voltage.

products.name: Greenworks Pro 60-Volt Max Lithium Ion 550-CFM 150-MPH Heavy-Duty
products.verdict: A heavy-duty 60V backpack blower with both CFM and MPH in the name.
products.description:
The Greenworks Pro 60-Volt is a backpack blower whose title lists 550 CFM and 150 MPH, with a lithium ion battery. It is priced in the $200 to $500 range.

It ranks last of the four because it matches the Greenworks 60V on airflow while the 40V model lists more. Its advantage is that it is the only one here that spells out an air speed of 150 MPH.

Pick it for stubborn debris where air speed matters. The caveat is that the same 550 CFM is available in the cheaper-sounding 60V model, so check that you value the speed figure.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want both airflow and air speed stated.
products.skipIf: You want the highest CFM in the group.

whatMatters.detail: CFM measures the volume of air the blower moves each minute. A higher figure clears wide piles faster, so it matters on larger lawns. Look for the number in the title or bullet points rather than a vague phrase like powerful airflow.

MPH describes how fast the air leaves the nozzle. High speed lifts wet or stuck debris that volume alone leaves behind. Few listings state it, so treat a published MPH figure as a useful extra detail.

Voltage sets which battery platform you are buying into. A 60V blower shares batteries with other 60V tools from the same brand, while a 40V does not. Check what tools you already own before choosing.
A backpack design moves weight from your arm to your shoulders and hips. That matters over long sessions. Confirm the listing says backpack, because some battery blowers are handheld.
Backpack blowers range widely in cost once batteries are included. Compare the price range shown and confirm whether the battery and charger come in the box before you buy.

faq.q: Do these blowers come with a battery?
faq.a: The listings we reviewed do not make this clear. Check the product page for whether the battery and charger are included before you order.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake when buying?
faq.a: Choosing on CFM alone. Air speed, battery platform and comfort all affect how the blower performs in practice.

faq.q: Is a 60V blower worth it over a 40V?
faq.a: Only if you own or plan to buy other 60V tools. On paper the 40V Greenworks lists more airflow than either 60V model here.

faq.q: How do I check airflow on a listing?
faq.a: Look for a CFM number in the title or bullet points. The WORX listing gives none, so confirm it on the product page.

faq.q: How should I care for the battery?
faq.a: Follow the manufacturer's guidance in the manual. Store it as directed and avoid leaving it fully drained for long periods.

faq.q: Can a backpack blower handle wet leaves?
faq.a: Air speed matters most for wet debris. Only the Greenworks Pro lists an MPH figure, at 150 MPH.

finalTake: For most yards the WORX Backpack Leaf Blower is the easy choice, with the Greenworks 40V the pick if airflow is the priority. The Greenworks 60V and Greenworks Pro 60-Volt suit buyers building around a 60V platform. Confirm battery and charger inclusion on the listing before buying.
